source_title: Stanford CS224N Winter 2026 Assignment 2, Part 3(e)(iii): Neural Transition-Based Dependency Parsing
chapter_or_section: Stanford CS224N Winter 2026 Assignment 2, Part 3(e)(iii): Neural Transition-Based Dependency Parsing
title: Neural Transition-Based Dependency Parsing — implement parser_model.py and run.py
instruction_text: In this section, you’ll be implementing a neural-network based dependency parser with the goal of maximizing performance on the UAS (Unlabeled Attachment Score) metric. First, the model extracts a feature vector representing the current state. This feature vector consists of a list of tokens w = [w1, w2, . . . , wm] where each 0 ≤ wi < |V| is the index of a token in the vocabulary. Then our network looks up an embedding for each word and concatenates them into a single input vector: x = [Ew1, ..., Ewm]. We then compute our prediction as: h = ReLU(xW + b1), l = hU + b2, ŷ = softmax(l). In parser_model.py you will find skeleton code to implement this simple neural network using PyTorch. Complete the init, embedding_lookup and forward functions to implement the model. Then complete the train_for_epoch and train functions within the run.py file. Finally execute python run.py to train your model and compute predictions on test data from Penn Treebank (annotated with Universal Dependencies).
expected_output: A working implementation of the neural dependency parser in parser_model.py and the training functions in run.py; train the model and report the best UAS on the dev set and the UAS on the test set.
constraints: Do not use torch.nn.Linear or torch.nn.Embedding in your code.
Follow naming requirements in the TODOs if any are explicitly specified.
Use efficient functions and avoid for loops when implementing embedding lookup.

test_cases.description: Debug mode; expected dev loss < 0.2 and dev UAS > 65.
Full training; expected train loss < 0.08 and dev UAS > 87.

learning_objectives: Implement embedding lookup from a token index feature vector.
Build a feedforward neural dependency parser in PyTorch.
Train and evaluate a transition-based parser with UAS.

source_title: PyTorch tutorial: Translation with a Sequence to Sequence Network and Attention / The Seq2Seq Model / The Encoder / The Decoder / Training the Model
chapter_or_section: PyTorch tutorial: Translation with a Sequence to Sequence Network and Attention / The Seq2Seq Model / The Encoder / The Decoder / Training the Model
title: The Seq2Seq Model: The Encoder and The Decoder
instruction_text:
Write your own classes and functions to preprocess the data for an NLP modeling task. In this project, you will teach a neural network to translate from French to English.

A Sequence to Sequence network, or seq2seq network, is a model consisting of two RNNs called the encoder and decoder. The encoder reads an input sequence and outputs a single vector, and the decoder reads that vector to produce an output sequence.

The encoder of a seq2seq network is a RNN that outputs a value for every word from the input sentence. For every input word the encoder outputs a vector and a hidden state, and uses the hidden state for the next input word.

The decoder is another RNN that takes the encoder output vector(s) and outputs a sequence of words to create the translation.

Teacher forcing is the concept of using the real target outputs as each next input, instead of using the decoder's guess as the next input.
expected_output: A sequence-to-sequence model that can translate from French to English.
learning_objectives: Implement an encoder and a decoder for a seq2seq model.
Explain the role of teacher forcing during training.
Build and train a PyTorch sequence-to-sequence translation model.

chapter_or_section: Keras Code Examples / NLP / Text classification / Bidirectional LSTM on IMDB
title: Build and train a 2-layer bidirectional LSTM on IMDB
instruction_text: Build a text classification model for the IMDB movie review sentiment dataset. Use an embedding layer followed by two bidirectional LSTM layers and a dense sigmoid classifier, then train and evaluate the model on padded review sequences.
starter_code:
max_features = 20000
maxlen = 200

inputs = keras.Input(shape=(None,), dtype="int32")
x = layers.Embedding(max_features, 128)(inputs)
x = layers.Bidirectional(layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences=True))(x)
x = layers.Bidirectional(layers.LSTM(64))(x)
outputs = layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid")(x)
model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs)

(x_train, y_train), (x_val, y_val) = keras.datasets.imdb.load_data(num_words=max_features)
x_train = keras.utils.pad_sequences(x_train, maxlen=maxlen)
x_val = keras.utils.pad_sequences(x_val, maxlen=maxlen)

model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="binary_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])
model.fit(x_train, y_train, batch_size=32, epochs=2, validation_data=(x_val, y_val))
expected_output: A trained Keras model for IMDB sentiment classification with validation accuracy and loss reported after training.
constraints: Use the IMDB dataset loaded with num_words=max_features.
Pad input sequences to maxlen=200.
Use two bidirectional LSTM layers.
Use a sigmoid output for binary sentiment classification.

Understand sequence modeling for sentiment classification.
Apply recurrent architectures to NLP tasks in Keras.

source_title: Keras Code Examples / Machine translation / Character-level recurrent sequence-to-sequence model
chapter_or_section: Keras Code Examples / Machine translation / Character-level recurrent sequence-to-sequence model
title: Implement a character-level recurrent seq2seq translator
instruction_text: Implement a basic character-level recurrent sequence-to-sequence model for translating short English sentences into short French sentences. Build an encoder LSTM that returns its final states, then build a decoder LSTM initialized with the encoder states, followed by a dense softmax layer. Train the model on vectorized character sequences and use the trained model for decoding.
starter_code:
encoder_inputs = keras.Input(shape=(None, num_encoder_tokens))
encoder = keras.layers.LSTM(latent_dim, return_state=True)
encoder_outputs, state_h, state_c = encoder(encoder_inputs)
encoder_states = [state_h, state_c]

decoder_inputs = keras.Input(shape=(None, num_decoder_tokens))
decoder_lstm = keras.layers.LSTM(latent_dim, return_sequences=True, return_state=True)
decoder_outputs, _, _ = decoder_lstm(decoder_inputs, initial_state=encoder_states)
decoder_dense = keras.layers.Dense(num_decoder_tokens, activation="softmax")
decoder_outputs = decoder_dense(decoder_outputs)

model = keras.Model([encoder_inputs, decoder_inputs], decoder_outputs)
model.compile(optimizer="rmsprop", loss="categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])
model.fit(
    [encoder_input_data, decoder_input_data],
    decoder_target_data,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    epochs=epochs,
    validation_split=0.2,
)
expected_output: A trained character-level seq2seq model that maps short English sentences to short French sentences and can be used for decoding at inference time.
constraints: Use a character-level encoder-decoder architecture.
Use an encoder LSTM with return_state=True.
Initialize the decoder LSTM with the encoder states.
Use a dense softmax layer over the decoder outputs.
learning_objectives: Understand the encoder-decoder formulation of recurrent sequence-to-sequence learning.
Implement teacher-forced seq2seq training with Keras.
Connect training-time seq2seq modeling with inference-time decoding.
course_context: Keras Code Examples / Machine translation / Character-level recurrent sequence-to-sequence model
